contentHtml:
Runtime names appear in deployment commands, routing, secret grants and recovery procedures. Favor stable service purpose over implementation detail.

Infrastructure Projects

An infrastructure project, account workspace or state boundary SHOULD follow:

<domain>-<purpose>[-<environment>]

platform-network-prod
platform-observability
portfolio-edge-stg

Include prod or stg when the project is an isolation, access-control, billing or state boundary. Omit it from shared tooling with explicit multi-environment scope.

Good                              Avoid
platform-network-prod             terraform-prod-final
platform-observability            misc-infra

Docker Swarm Stacks

A stack is the environment-scoped application deployment unit:

<system>-<environment>

orders-prod
orders-stg
observability-prod

Docker Swarm prefixes deployed service, network and volume names with the stack name. Therefore, use concise logical service names inside the stack:

services:
  api:
  worker:
  db:

Resulting operator-visible service names include orders-prod_api and orders-prod_worker. The underscore is generated by Swarm; it is not the preferred delimiter for manually named runtime resources.

Good Avoid Reason
Stack orders-prod, service api Stack prod, service orders-api-prod Avoid duplication and retain ownership
Stack observability-prod Stack obs1 Readable during incidents

Services

Outside a namespace or stack that already supplies system scope, use:

<system>-<component>

orders-api
orders-worker
portfolio-web

Inside a scoped stack or Kubernetes application boundary, the short component name MAY be used if tooling and dashboards preserve the parent identity.

Service names MUST remain stable through releases. Use image tags and telemetry attributes for version, and labels for environment or instance detail.

Networks

Name networks by trust boundary or traffic purpose, not implementation:

<scope>-<purpose>[-<environment>]

edge-public-prod
orders-private-prod
observability-monitoring-prod
Good Avoid Reason
edge-public-prod traefik-net-new Purpose survives proxy replacement
orders-data-prod network2 Reveals permitted traffic class

An externally shared ingress network should carry a platform scope such as edge, not the name of a single consuming application.

Secrets

Secret object identifiers MUST be safe to show in configuration, logs and access reviews; secret values never belong in names.

<system>-<consumer>-<credential>[-<environment>]

orders-api-db-password-prod
orders-api-jwt-signing-key-prod
edge-proxy-dns-token-prod

Include the environment if the secret store or cluster may contain more than one environment. Map secret objects into concise runtime variables:

Secret object: orders-api-db-password-prod
Application key: DATABASE_PASSWORD

Avoid names that expose account identifiers, actual hosts, employee names or rotation history:

Avoid
password-for-carlos
db-password-new-final
aws-key-AKIA...

Rotation replaces secret content or a controlled version reference; it should not cause unbounded naming drift.

Domains and Subdomains

DNS names use lowercase labels separated by .. Use subdomain hierarchy to express endpoint and environment:

Production:      api.example.com
Staging:         api.stg.example.com
Preview:         pr-184.preview.example.com
Operations:      grafana.ops.example.com

Do not place prod in the public production URL unless multiple production realms genuinely require disambiguation. Users and integrations should see the canonical endpoint.

Good                              Avoid
api.stg.example.com               api_staging.example.com
grafana.ops.example.com           new-grafana-prod-final.example.com

Hosts and Cluster Nodes

Physical or virtual nodes need stable infrastructure identity, independent of the workloads scheduled on them:

<location>-<platform>-<role>-<ordinal>

br-sp1-swarm-manager-01
br-sp1-swarm-worker-03
us-east1-runner-linux-02

Use a documented region or site code and zero-padded ordinals where multiple nodes exist. Do not name nodes after the current application, IP address or an individual. A node may host different services over its lifetime.

When represented as Kubernetes Node objects, these names remain compatible with DNS-subdomain naming constraints.
